Check whether a dataset's roxygen2 documentation is up to date

Source: R/update.R
sd_check_documentation_current.Rd

A fast, LLM-free diagnostic: compares the variable names in x against the variables already documented in the existing roxygen2 file (parsed from its \describe{} block), and reports any that are missing. Run this any time you suspect a dataset has grown new variables since it was last documented – if it finds any, follow up with sd_update_roxygen().

Usage

sd_check_documentation_current(x, object_name, file = NULL)

Arguments

x

An sd_data object.

object_name

Name the documented object has, e.g. "survey_data" – the same name used with sd_generate_roxygen().

file

Path to the existing roxygen2 file. Defaults to file.path("R", paste0(object_name, ".R")), matching sd_generate_roxygen()'s default.

Value

Invisibly, a character vector of variable names present in x but not found in file's \describe{} block (empty if none). Called for its printed message.

Details

Because sd_document()'s descriptive text is based on the same underlying data, undocumented variables here are also a signal that the sd_document() text may be stale and worth regenerating.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
sd_check_documentation_current(aineisto, "survey_data")
} # }
